summary: One SetEvent on a non-signaled auto-reset event with two pending timed waiters releases exactly one of them; which one is not fixed; the event is non-signaled afterwards.
applicability: windows_reference: Windows 10/11 x86-64 user mode; kernel32 SetEvent and WaitForSingleObject on an unnamed auto-reset event created non-signaled

initial.event: CreateEventW(NULL, FALSE, FALSE, NULL) by main

execution.main: after both waiters are pending: SetEvent(event) once; then WaitForSingleObject(thread_a) and WaitForSingleObject(thread_b); then WaitForSingleObject(event, 0)

evidence.applicability: all Windows versions the page covers
evidence.quote: An event object whose state remains signaled until a single waiting thread is released, at which time the system automatically sets the state to nonsignaled. If no threads are waiting, the event object's state remains signaled. If more than one thread is waiting, a waiting thread is selected. Do not assume a first-in, first-out (FIFO) order. External events such as kernel-mode APCs can change the wait order.
WAIT_OBJECT_0 0x00000000L The state of the specified object is signaled. WAIT_TIMEOUT 0x00000102L The time-out interval elapsed, and the object's state is nonsignaled.

evidence.source_ref: reasoning: with a 2000 ms timeout far above signal latency, the released waiter returns WAIT_OBJECT_0 and the other returns WAIT_TIMEOUT, so the selected waiter is observable through GUEST_CALL_RETURNED without an object-state tag
evidence.distinguishing_check: reference runs of the probe: every run shows exactly one waiter returning 0 and the other 258, and main's zero-timeout wait returning 258; a run where both time out or both return 0 refutes it

open_questions: Does an APC delivered to a waiter during the wait change which waiter is selected (the page says it can change wait order)? Needs an alertable-wait variant.
Is the 2000 ms timeout safe on a loaded hosted runner? A timed-out run that should have been released would look like the forbidden empty outcome.

sections.state: event: {signaled: bool}; waiters: ordered-by-nothing set of pending threads
sections.transitions: SetEvent with >=1 pending waiter: release exactly one waiter, signaled stays false; with none: signaled := true
sections.nondeterminism: which pending waiter is released (allowed outcome set)
sections.ordering: the released waiter's wait return happens-after the SetEvent call (hb edge main:SetEvent -> waiter:return)
sections.progress: the released waiter returns before its timeout under the scheduler assumption that a released thread runs within 2000 ms
sections.allowed_optimizations: the implementation may choose either waiter by any policy, including always the same one
